Epic Description: Establish the core repo, tooling, infrastructure, LLM plumbing, configuration and observability needed for all later RAG work.
Feature Description: Create project repository and CI/CD pipeline to build, test and deploy the RAG service to a development environment.
Acceptance Criteria: Git repository created with basic branching rules and code ownership ; CI runs lint and tests on each pull request ; Docker image built reproducibly in CI ; Hello-world service deploys automatically to dev from main branch ; README documents local development and CI/CD workflow
Dependencies: None (project kickoff)

Epic Description: Establish the core repo, tooling, infrastructure, LLM plumbing, configuration and observability needed for all later RAG work.
Feature Description: Integrate chosen LLM provider and configure LangChain primitives for chat and embeddings.
Acceptance Criteria: At least one chat model and one embedding model configured via environment variables or secret manager ; Simple healthcheck endpoint or script calls the LLM and returns a response ; LangChain wrappers for LLM and embeddings implemented and unit-tested ; Timeouts and authentication errors handled gracefully ; Configuration (models, rate limits, env vars) documented
Dependencies: Repo & CI/CD baseline

Epic Description: Establish the core repo, tooling, infrastructure, LLM plumbing, configuration and observability needed for all later RAG work.
Feature Description: Implement configuration management, basic internal authentication and structured logging/metrics.
Acceptance Criteria: Configuration handled via env/config files with no secrets in code ; Secrets (API keys, DB credentials) stored securely and rotation procedure documented ; Internal authentication (e.g., shared token or SSO placeholder) enforced on API endpoints ; Structured logs emitted with correlation IDs and response times ; Basic metrics (request count, latency, error rate) exposed or logged
Dependencies: LLM + LangChain baseline ; Repo & CI/CD baseline

Epic Description: Deliver a usable 'chat with our documents' MVP over a limited corpus using Chroma and a simple RAG chain.
Feature Description: Build a batch ingestion job to parse a pilot set of documents and split them into heuristic chunks with metadata.
Acceptance Criteria: Supported document formats defined (e.g., PDF, DOCX, Markdown) ; Documents from a configured location parsed into clean text with document-level metadata (title, path, timestamp) ; Heuristic chunking implemented (e.g., 300 500 token chunks) ; Failed parses logged without crashing the ingestion run ; Pipeline can be rerun idempotently for the same corpus
Dependencies: E1   Foundations & Environment

Epic Description: Deliver a usable 'chat with our documents' MVP over a limited corpus using Chroma and a simple RAG chain.
Feature Description: Deploy Chroma, define collection schema and index chunks with embeddings and metadata.
Acceptance Criteria: Chroma instance running locally or in a container with persistence enabled ; Embeddings computed for all chunks using chosen embedding model ; Chunks stored with metadata (doc_id, source, creation time, ACL placeholders) ; Test query against Chroma returns reasonable top-k chunks for sample questions ; Indexing job can be rerun without duplicating records
Dependencies: Ingestion pipeline v1 (parsing & chunking) ; LLM + LangChain baseline

Epic Description: Deliver a usable 'chat with our documents' MVP over a limited corpus using Chroma and a simple RAG chain.
Feature Description: Implement a LangChain RAG chain (Chroma retriever plus generator) and expose it via a REST endpoint.
Acceptance Criteria: Given a question, the chain retrieves top-k chunks from Chroma and calls the LLM to generate an answer ; Answers include at least doc_id and section title as citations ; Prompt template instructs model to answer only from provided context or say I don't know ; REST endpoint POST /rag/query returns answer and cited sources ; Unit and integration tests exist for a set of pilot questions
Dependencies: Chroma setup & vector index ; Config, auth & observability baseline

Epic Description: Deliver a usable 'chat with our documents' MVP over a limited corpus using Chroma and a simple RAG chain.
Feature Description: Build a simple web UI and a small evaluation set to test the MVP end-to-end.
Acceptance Criteria: Single-page UI or simple front-end allows interactive questions and shows answer plus sources ; 20 30 test questions defined for the pilot corpus ; Manual evaluation pass performed and results recorded ; Key failure modes captured as backlog items for later epics
Dependencies: Simple RAG chain + REST API

Epic Description: Extend the ingestion layer so DOC/DOCX are handled as unstructured documents and CSV/XLSX as structured/tabular data while reusing the existing Unstructured and Structured agents.
Feature Description: Add support in the ingestion pipeline for .doc and .docx files and route them into the existing unstructured document flow.
Acceptance Criteria: Ingestion job detects DOC/DOCX via file extension or MIME type ; DOC/DOCX files parsed into text with basic structure (headings, paragraphs) ; Parsed DOC/DOCX normalized into the same internal Document model used for PDFs ; DOC/DOCX content passes through chunking, embedding, Chroma indexing and lexical indexing ; At least 5 10 sample DOC/DOCX files ingested and retrievable via the Docs Agent
Dependencies: E2   Document RAG MVP

Epic Description: Extend the ingestion layer so DOC/DOCX are handled as unstructured documents and CSV/XLSX as structured/tabular data while reusing the existing Unstructured and Structured agents.
Feature Description: Implement classification logic to decide whether a CSV/XLSX file should be treated as structured table data or as a report-like unstructured document.
Acceptance Criteria: Ingestion detects .csv and .xlsx and loads them into an intermediate DataFrame representation ; Heuristics (row/column counts, numeric cell ratio, long-text presence) classify sheets as tabular or report_like ; Classification decisions logged and overridable via configuration ; Manual review of a sample set shows classification is reasonable for the majority of cases
Dependencies: Ingestion pipeline v1 (parsing & chunking)

Epic Description: Extend the ingestion layer so DOC/DOCX are handled as unstructured documents and CSV/XLSX as structured/tabular data while reusing the existing Unstructured and Structured agents.
Feature Description: For sheets classified as tabular, load them into a SQL store as tables with metadata linking back to the original file.
Acceptance Criteria: Tabular CSV/XLSX sheets mapped to DB table names using a consistent naming convention ; Columns typed (string, numeric, date) based on inference or config ; Tables loaded into the DB idempotently so re-ingestion updates or replaces data without duplication ; Metadata catalog links file and sheet to table name and domain labels ; Several real CSV/XLSX files loaded and queryable via SQL
Dependencies: Spreadsheet classifier (tabular vs report-like) ; Config, auth & observability baseline

Epic Description: Extend the ingestion layer so DOC/DOCX are handled as unstructured documents and CSV/XLSX as structured/tabular data while reusing the existing Unstructured and Structured agents.
Feature Description: For sheets classified as report_like, convert them into a textual representation and route them into the unstructured document pipeline.
Acceptance Criteria: Report-like sheets rendered into human-readable text or Markdown-style tables with headers and notes ; Flattened spreadsheet text wrapped in the same Document structure as other unstructured sources ; Flattened documents pass through chunking, embedding, Chroma and lexical indexing ; Representative report-like spreadsheets retrievable via the Docs Agent with understandable content
Dependencies: Spreadsheet classifier (tabular vs report-like) ; DOC/DOCX parsing & ingestion

Epic Description: Extend the ingestion layer so DOC/DOCX are handled as unstructured documents and CSV/XLSX as structured/tabular data while reusing the existing Unstructured and Structured agents.
Feature Description: Build a lightweight dataset catalog for tabular sources and generate short natural-language summaries that can be indexed in Chroma to support discovery.
Acceptance Criteria: Catalog tracks all tabular datasets with table name, origin file, domain, owner, update time and row count ; For each tabular dataset an LLM generates a short summary describing columns and contents ; Summaries indexed in Chroma as dataset documents with metadata linking back to underlying tables ; Users can ask high-level questions about available data and receive dataset summaries pointing to relevant tables ; Cost controls and error handling in place for summary generation
Dependencies: Tabular CSV/XLSX → SQL ingestion ; LLM + LangChain baseline

Epic Description: Improve answer quality via hybrid (semantic plus lexical) retrieval and add a structured SQL agent with basic routing.
Feature Description: Integrate a lexical/BM25 search layer over the same document corpus used by Chroma.
Acceptance Criteria: All chunks indexed in a lexical engine or Chroma full-text index with IDs linking back to vector entries ; API wrapper allows running keyword queries and mapping results back to document chunks ; Sanity tests show better results on keyword-heavy queries (IDs, exact names) than vector-only ; Indexing job handles updates and removals without stale entries
Dependencies: Chroma setup & vector index ; Config, auth & observability baseline

Epic Description: Improve answer quality via hybrid (semantic plus lexical) retrieval and add a structured SQL agent with basic routing.
Feature Description: Combine semantic and lexical results and rerank with a cross-encoder before passing context to the LLM.
Acceptance Criteria: Hybrid retriever implemented with configurable weights between vector and lexical scores ; Cross-encoder reranking reorders merged candidates and selects final top-k context chunks ; Offline comparison on test questions shows hybrid plus reranker outperforms vector-only and lexical-only baselines in relevance ; Latency for hybrid retrieval and reranking measured and within agreed thresholds
Dependencies: Lexical search + index ; Chroma setup & vector index

Epic Description: Improve answer quality via hybrid (semantic plus lexical) retrieval and add a structured SQL agent with basic routing.
Feature Description: Integrate Postgres or chosen SQL DB and implement a LangChain SQL agent with guardrails.
Acceptance Criteria: Read-only DB connection configured and health-checked from the service ; Key tables and schemas documented and included in  SQL prompts ;  SQL chain correctly answers a representative set of questions against the database ; Queries restricted to safe SELECT-only operations with graceful handling of invalid or ambiguous requests
Dependencies: Config, auth & observability baseline ; Tabular CSV/XLSX → SQL ingestion

Epic Description: Improve answer quality via hybrid (semantic plus lexical) retrieval and add a structured SQL agent with basic routing.
Feature Description: Add a simple router to choose between docs, SQL or both and apply basic ACL filters for both RAG and SQL queries.
Acceptance Criteria: Rule-based or light LLM-based classifier distinguishes document-centric from data-centric questions ; Routing decisions logged for later analysis ; Document metadata includes basic ACL attributes and retrieval filters by user or role when provided ; SQL agent restricted to role-appropriate schemas and tables and unauthorized access is denied and logged
Dependencies: SQL DB integration +  SQL agent ; Lexical search + index

Epic Description: Replace ad-hoc composition with a LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestrator and introduce a Self-RAG-style critic and bounded refinement loop plus telemetry.
Feature Description: Model the RAG workflow as a LangGraph state machine with nodes for router, agents, synthesis and critic.
Acceptance Criteria: Graph state defined including question, evidence, partial answers and control flags ; Nodes implemented for Router, Docs Agent, SQL Agent, Answer Synthesizer and Critic ; End-to-end RAG flow runs through the LangGraph entry point instead of ad-hoc chaining ; Errors in individual nodes produce traceable failures without corrupting global state
Dependencies: Hybrid retriever & reranker ; SQL DB integration +  SQL agent

Epic Description: Replace ad-hoc composition with a LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestrator and introduce a Self-RAG-style critic and bounded refinement loop plus telemetry.
Feature Description: Wire existing agents into the orchestrator and define robust state passing between nodes.
Acceptance Criteria: Shared state type used across nodes and validated on read/write ; Each node reads and writes only its relevant fields in the state ; Router can send a question to docs, SQL or both and aggregate evidence into state ; Existing API endpoints now invoke the orchestrator graph rather than stand-alone chains
Dependencies: Orchestrator graph skeleton (LangGraph)

Epic Description: Replace ad-hoc composition with a LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestrator and introduce a Self-RAG-style critic and bounded refinement loop plus telemetry.
Feature Description: Implement an LLM-based critic that evaluates support, relevance and usefulness and triggers one refinement cycle when needed.
Acceptance Criteria: Critic prompt defined to accept question, candidate answer and evidence and return structured JSON including support level and needs_new_retrieval flag ; Critic node integrated into the graph and invoked after initial answer generation ; Orchestrator supports one additional retrieval and regeneration iteration when needs_new_retrieval is true with hard bounds on loop depth ; Regression tests show improved grounding or safe I don't know responses for previously unsupported answers
Dependencies: Multi-agent state & integration ; Hybrid retriever & reranker

Epic Description: Replace ad-hoc composition with a LangGraph-based multi-agent orchestrator and introduce a Self-RAG-style critic and bounded refinement loop plus telemetry.
Feature Description: Capture detailed traces of runs and build a simple pipeline to compute RAG quality metrics.
Acceptance Criteria: For each query, store question, selected context, final answer, critic decision and latency metrics ; A small labeled dataset of queries and gold answers created for offline evaluation ; Script or notebook computes basic RAG metrics such as faithfulness and relevance on the labeled set ; Simple report or dashboard summarizes quality over time and per epic or release
Dependencies: Config, auth & observability baseline ; Orchestrator graph skeleton (LangGraph)

Epic Description: Introduce a Neo4j knowledge graph, a graph agent and advanced ingestion (agentic and hierarchical chunking) plus an optional web/external agent.
Feature Description: Provision Neo4j instances and define the initial graph schema for key entities and relationships.
Acceptance Criteria: Neo4j deployed in a development environment with connectivity from the RAG service ; Graph schema designed for at least one priority domain such as products, clients or contracts ; Basic Cypher queries validate schema and connectivity ; Backup and restore approach documented even if initially manual
Dependencies: E1   Foundations & Environment ; domain model input from stakeholders

Epic Description: Introduce a Neo4j knowledge graph, a graph agent and advanced ingestion (agentic and hierarchical chunking) plus an optional web/external agent.
Feature Description: Implement a pipeline to extract entities and relations from documents or structured sources and populate Neo4j.
Acceptance Criteria: Extraction approach defined using LLM prompts and/or NER models ; Pipeline processes a subset of documents and outputs candidate entities and relations with confidence scores ; Deduplication and merging strategy implemented for entities appearing under different names ; Initial knowledge graph for one domain loaded into Neo4j and queryable with meaningful content
Dependencies: Neo4j infra & schema ; Ingestion pipeline v1 (parsing & chunking)

Epic Description: Introduce a Neo4j knowledge graph, a graph agent and advanced ingestion (agentic and hierarchical chunking) plus an optional web/external agent.
Feature Description: Implement a graph agent that uses Neo4j to answer graph-style queries and restrict RAG search space.
Acceptance Criteria: LangChain Neo4j or graph chain configured to generate and execute Cypher queries from natural language ; Representative graph-style questions answered plausibly using Neo4j ; Graph agent integrated as a node in the orchestrator graph ; Knowledge graph query results can be used to filter documents or rows before RAG retrieval when appropriate
Dependencies: Entity & relation extraction + KG population ; Orchestrator graph skeleton (LangGraph)

Epic Description: Introduce a Neo4j knowledge graph, a graph agent and advanced ingestion (agentic and hierarchical chunking) plus an optional web/external agent.
Feature Description: Replace heuristic chunking with LLM-guided chunking and hierarchical summaries for large documents.
Acceptance Criteria: LLM-based chunker implemented that respects document structure such as headings and sections ; Hierarchical metadata stored linking documents to section summaries to fine-grained chunks ; Retrieval can operate at summary level but fetch underlying detailed chunks for answer context ; Offline tests show improved retrieval quality or latency compared to the initial heuristic chunking

Epic Description: Introduce a Neo4j knowledge graph, a graph agent and advanced ingestion (agentic and hierarchical chunking) plus an optional web/external agent.
Feature Description: Add a constrained web/external agent for approved domains or APIs, integrated into the orchestrator.
Acceptance Criteria: Web or external agent implemented with domain allowlist and strict timeout limits ; External content normalized into the same evidence format including source, snippet, URL and timestamp ; Orchestrator can optionally call the web agent when internal sources are insufficient and configuration allows it ; Governance and compliance rules for external sources documented and applied
Dependencies: Orchestrator graph skeleton (LangGraph) ; Config, auth & observability baseline
